name: KIVI — 2-bit KV cache quantisation

source.title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache

oneLiner: Per-channel keys, per-token values, 2 bits — the 'quantise' branch of the KV bill (FP8/INT8 KV is now standard in vLLM / TensorRT-LLM).
whyFootnote: Numerics rather than an attention mechanism.

name: LongRoPE — searched non-uniform interpolation to 2M

source.title: LongRoPE: Extending LLM Context Window Beyond 2 Million Tokens

problem: Pretrained RoPE models were stuck at ~128K: long-length fine-tuning is expensive, long text is scarce, new positions produce catastrophic values.
idea: Search (evolutionary, seeded with PI/NTK/YaRN) per-dimension rescale factors and a 'first n tokens interpolated less' rule; extend progressively 256K → 2,048K with ≤1K fine-tuning steps; readjust at 8K to recover short-context quality.
buys: 2,048K nominal window on LLaMA-2 / Mistral with ~1K steps; 8× with no fine-tuning; only the PE changes, so FlashAttention is reused
Phi-3's route to 128K
costs: Search cost and a three-stage recipe; perplexity degrades noticeably at 2M and passkey retrieval drops
Does nothing about the compute or KV memory of *running* 2M tokens

agent1m.why: nominal window yes; recall at 1M no; KV cost untouched

pickWhen.verdict: The most elaborate way to stretch RoPE. If you can pretrain, Llama 3.1's base+staged route is safer.

name: Dual Chunk Attention (DCA)

source.title: Training-Free Long-Context Scaling of Large Language Models

firstShipped.model: Qwen2 Instruct (128K via YaRN + DCA; blog 2024-06-07, report 2407.10671 §3.2); Qwen2.5-1M later made DCA+YaRN the default

problem: Extrapolate a strong RoPE model at inference with no training, past where NTK/YaRN hold.
idea: Split the sequence into chunks and remap intra-, inter- and successive-chunk relative positions so none exceeds the trained range; FlashAttention-compatible.
buys: Llama-2-70B to 100K+ zero-shot; shipped in Qwen2 (Jun 2024) and Qwen2.5-1M (to reach 1M from 256K training)
costs: Coarse positions across chunks; three attention passes → extra prefill compute
Below true long-context training on hard retrieval

agent1m.why: the industrial way to get 4× more nominal context at inference only

pickWhen.verdict: The industrial successor of ReRoPE / SelfExtend.

name: Massive Activations in LLMs (why sinks exist)

source.title: Massive Activations in Large Language Models

oneLiner: 1e4–1e5× outlier activations at fixed positions act as bias terms and pull attention onto them — the mechanism behind attention sinks; explicit learnable attention biases remove them.
whyFootnote: Analysis, not a mechanism — but it explains why gpt-oss's learned sink works.

name: Griffin / RecurrentGemma

source.title: Griffin: Mixing Gated Linear Recurrences with Local Attention for Efficient Language Models

oneLiner: Gated linear recurrences interleaved with local attention; shipped as RecurrentGemma — an early local-attention + recurrence hybrid from a frontier lab.
whyFootnote: Represented on the timeline by the GLA / Mamba / hybrid nodes.

name: Jamba — first production Transformer–Mamba–MoE hybrid

source.title: Jamba: A Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Language Model
source.evidence: [v1] Thu, 28 Mar 2024 23:55:06 UTC (blog the same day)

oneLiner: 52B total / 12B active, 256K context on one 80 GB GPU — the first production hybrid, and the proof that a few attention layers rescue Mamba's recall.
whyFootnote: A model, not a mechanism; recorded as Mamba's first ship.

name: Infini-attention — compressive memory beside local attention

source.title: Leave No Context Behind: Efficient Infinite Context Transformers with Infini-attention

idea: Local softmax attention within a segment plus a linear-attention-style associative memory (delta-rule update, σ(Q)·M retrieval), mixed by a gate; constant memory and compute per segment.
buys: 1M-token passkey after fine-tuning at 5K (claimed); 114× memory compression; streaming inference
costs: Compressive memory is lossy (linear-attention capacity); reproductions weak; no released model
Segment-recurrent training complexity

pickWhen.verdict: Transformer-XL's recurrence reborn as a delta-rule memory — the bridge between softmax attention and the DeltaNet view.

name: SnapKV — prompt KV compression

source.title: SnapKV: LLM Knows What You are Looking for Before Generation

problem: For long-document QA the prompt's KV dwarfs the generation; select what to keep *before* decoding.
idea: Use the last-window ('observation') queries' attention per head, pooled, to keep clustered important positions.
buys: ~3.6× decode speedup, ~8.2× memory at 16K; no fine-tuning
costs: Selection depends on the end-of-prompt query — multi-turn or a new question may need evicted context
Per-head irregular retention complicates paged kernels; retrieval degrades at aggressive ratios

rag32k.why: single-turn long-context QA where prompt ≫ output

pickWhen.verdict: The prefill-side eviction; pairs with H2O (decode) and DuoAttention (per head).

name: MLA — Multi-head Latent Attention (DeepSeek-V2)
aka: low-rank joint KV compression with decoupled RoPE

source.title: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model
source.evidence: GitHub README news: '2024.05.06: We released the DeepSeek-V2.' — the model shipped one day before the report; arXiv [v1] Tue, 7 May 2024 15:56:43 UTC

secondary.label: DeepSeek-V3 reuses MLA ('thoroughly validated in DeepSeek-V2')
TransMLA — converting GQA checkpoints to MLA

firstShipped.model: DeepSeek-V2 (236B / 21B active, 128K); then V3, R1, V3.2

problem: At 128K the KV cache — even with GQA — decides batch size and throughput. Wanted MHA-or-better quality with a *smaller-than-GQA* cache.
idea: Project each token's K and V jointly into a small latent c (d_c = 512) and cache only that; up-project on the fly — and because W^UK can be absorbed into W^Q (and W^UV into W^O), attention runs in latent space at decode. RoPE breaks the absorption, so a separate 'decoupled' rotary key (d_h^R = 64) is carried alongside.
buys: Per-token cache (512 + 64) per layer ≈ 4.5 d_h — 'equal to GQA with only 2.25 groups'; DeepSeek claims 93.3% KV reduction and 5.76× generation throughput vs their 67B GQA model, at quality above MHA
The compress branch of the KV bill (vs share = GQA, evict = H2O, quantise = KIVI)
The base DeepSeek Sparse Attention (2025) is built on
costs: RoPE and low-rank absorption fight: the decoupled RoPE dimension is a workaround, not a feature
Extra up-projection FLOPs at prefill; needs bespoke decode kernels (FlashMLA); one latent shared across heads makes tensor-parallel KV sharding awkward
Not a retrofit (TransMLA later tries); co-tuned with DeepSeekMoE so gains are hard to isolate

chatbot2k.why: GQA already fits; MLA is more machinery than you need

coding128k.why: large batch, long context, you own pretraining and kernels

agent1m.why: the smallest exact-attention KV cache at MHA-level quality in production (plain MQA is smaller, at a quality cost)

pickWhen.verdict: Right when you train from scratch at scale and decode is KV-bound; wrong for small models where GQA is enough — and note the price is a kernel team.

name: YOCO — You Only Cache Once

source.title: You Only Cache Once: Decoder-Decoder Architectures for Language Models

oneLiner: A self-decoder produces one global KV read by all cross-decoder layers — KV ≈ 1/L, prefill can early-exit. Sibling of CLA.
whyFootnote: Folded into the CLA node (the layer axis of KV compression).

name: Cross-Layer Attention (CLA) — share KV across layers

source.title: Reducing Transformer Key-Value Cache Size with Cross-Layer Attention

firstShipped.model: Character.AI production models (KV tied between neighbouring layers, with MQA + local/global)

problem: MQA/GQA shrink the *head* axis of the KV cache; the *layer* axis is untouched.
idea: Share K/V between adjacent layers (CLA2 / CLA3), on top of MQA/GQA.
buys: ~2× smaller KV at near-identical perplexity on top of MQA; more batch per GPU
costs: Must be trained in; small quality hit; layers lose independent K/V
Benefit shrinks if you already use MLA / latent KV

coding128k.why: own pretraining, memory-bound — the Character.AI recipe

pickWhen.verdict: The other axis of KV compression, the same month as MLA.

name: CoPE — Contextual Position Encoding

source.title: Contextual Position Encoding: Learning to Count What's Important

oneLiner: Positions counted by content-gated increments (count sentences, not tokens) — a quality/counting idea, not a bill item.
whyFootnote: Not shipped; quality rather than cost.

name: Mamba-2 / State Space Duality — SSMs *are* linear attention

source.title: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality

firstShipped.model: Codestral Mamba 7B (Mistral) — 'based on the Mamba2 architecture'

problem: Mamba-1's selective scan is not tensor-core friendly and limits state size; and the linear-attention ↔ RNN link had not been made exact for SSMs.
idea: SSMs and masked linear attention are two views of structured semiseparable matrices. The SSD layer computes the recurrence with chunked matmuls — 2–8× faster than Mamba-1's scan, much larger state (N=64–256).
buys: Unifies the two efficiency threads in one theorem; tensor-parallel and sequence-parallel friendly
Competitive with Transformers on LM at tested scales; the layer inside Nemotron-H / Falcon-H1 hybrids
costs: Scalar per-head decay is less expressive than Mamba-1's per-channel gate
Still trails softmax on exact recall (Gated DeltaNet later beats it); deployments use hybrids

agent1m.why: the cheap layer of a hybrid

pickWhen.verdict: After SSD there is one linear thread, not two — and Gated DeltaNet is its next step.

name: DeltaNet made parallel — chunkwise WY training

source.title: Parallelizing Linear Transformers with the Delta Rule over Sequence Length
source.authors: Yang, Wang, Zhang, Shen, Kim (MIT / Soochow / IBM)

problem: The 2021 delta rule recalls better than additive linear attention but its update is sequential over the sequence, so it never scaled on GPUs.
idea: Write the product of the (I − β k kᵀ) Householder-like updates in a memory-efficient WY representation and train chunkwise, tensor-core style — the FlashLinearAttention recipe applied to the delta rule.
buys: DeltaNet at 1.3B / 100B tokens beats Mamba and GLA on perplexity and zero-shot; hybrids (DeltaNet + sliding window every other layer, or + two global layers) beat strong Transformer baselines
Constant per-token state; the training algorithm Gated DeltaNet and Kimi Delta Attention build on
costs: No forgetting gate — erase happens only through the delta update — so weaker length extrapolation than gated variants
Still below softmax on retrieval-heavy tasks; within-chunk sequential part; L2-normalised keys and β add constraints

agent1m.why: in practice you pick Gated DeltaNet, six months later

pickWhen.verdict: The paper that turned a 2021 idea into something trainable — the delta rule's second launch.

name: Quest — query-aware KV-page selection

source.title: Quest: Query-Aware Sparsity for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
source.authors: Tang, Zhao, Zhu, Xiao, Kasikci, Han (SJTU / MIT / UW / NVIDIA)

problem: Decode at long context is bottlenecked by loading the whole KV cache per query; eviction (H2O, sinks) drops tokens permanently, but which tokens matter depends on the query.
idea: Keep min/max key values per KV page, upper-bound each page's score for the current query, load only the top-K pages. Nothing is dropped.
buys: Up to 7× self-attention speedup at 32K (2K-token budget); the 2.2× end-to-end figure is measured with 4-bit weights; training-free
costs: Full KV still stored — bandwidth, not memory, is saved
Upper bound can pick wrong pages; budget per task; awkward with GQA (query heads sharing a KV head want different pages); no gain at short context — it is built on paged KV by design

rag32k.why: latency-bound decode where HBM capacity is fine but bandwidth is not

pickWhen.verdict: Top-k attention finally with a cheap index (page bounds) — the training-free step before NSA / DSA.

name: Gemma 2 — interleaved local (4K window) / global layers

source.title: Gemma 2: Improving Open Language Models at a Practical Size
source.evidence: Google blog dated Jun 27, 2024; paper [v1] Wed, 31 Jul 2024 19:13:07 UTC — 'The sliding window size of local attention layers is set to 4096 tokens, while the span of the global attention layers is set to 8192 tokens'

problem: KV memory and attention compute per token for a mid-size open model, without giving up a global receptive field.
idea: Alternate sliding-window layers (w = 4,096) with global layers; only half the layers' KV grows with context. Plus GQA and logit soft-capping.
buys: Halves the layers whose cache grows; the local:global pattern Gemma 3 pushes to 5:1 and gpt-oss adopts as banded:dense
costs: At an 8K context the saving is modest; local layers are blind beyond the window
Needs SWA-capable kernels; soft-capping was initially incompatible with FlashAttention

chatbot2k.why: harmless, but at ≤4K every local layer is a full layer

coding128k.why: the design gets more valuable as context grows

agent1m.why: the global layers still pay n²; pair with sparse selection

pickWhen.verdict: Not the first sliding-window model (Mistral), nor the first to interleave — GPT-3 alternated dense and banded layers, and Character.AI described 1 global per 6 layers a week earlier — but the first open-weights model to make interleaving the headline design that Gemma 3 and gpt-oss copied.

name: MInference — dynamic sparse prefill

source.title: MInference 1.0: Accelerating Pre-filling for Long-Context LLMs via Dynamic Sparse Attention

problem: Prefill at 100K–1M tokens takes minutes on dense attention; per-head attention is dynamically sparse.
idea: Offline assign each head one of three patterns (A-shape, vertical-slash, block-sparse), build the sparse index online, run custom kernels.
buys: Up to 10× prefill speedup at 1M with near-lossless accuracy, no retraining
costs: Prefill only; per-model pattern search; approximate index overhead
Superseded by trained sparsity (NSA / DSA)

agent1m.why: serving an existing dense model at very long prompts

pickWhen.verdict: The training-free precursor to NSA / MoBA / DSA.

name: Llama 3.1 — 128K by 'llama3' RoPE scaling + staged long-context pretraining (base 500K unchanged from Llama 3)

source.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
source.evidence: Meta blog dated July 23, 2024; paper [v1] 31 Jul 2024; config.json rope_scaling {rope_type 'llama3', factor 8, low_freq_factor 1, high_freq_factor 4, original_max_position_embeddings 8192}, rope_theta 500000; 'increased context length gradually in six stages … ending in the final 128K'

problem: Take dense 8K models to 128K with no architecture change.
idea: Keep Llama 3's base 500K (already the 8K models' setting), add the 'llama3' wavelength-dependent scaling (high-frequency dims untouched, low-frequency ÷ 8, ramp between), and ~800B tokens of continued pretraining in six length stages — the 128K came from the scaling + training, not from raising the base.
buys: The safest, no-architecture-risk path to 128K; the numbers in every Llama-family config.json
costs: Not free: ~800B tokens
Attention compute and KV at 128K unchanged (only GQA helps); nothing beyond 128K

coding128k.why: if you can spend ~8×10¹¹ tokens of continued pretraining

pickWhen.verdict: What 'RoPE scaling' means in production: not a trick, a training recipe.

name: Sigmoid attention (FlashSigmoid)

source.title: Theory, Analysis, and Best Practices for Sigmoid Self-Attention

oneLiner: softmax → sigmoid with a fused kernel 17% faster than FA2 on H100 and parity claims; not adopted.

name: Differential Transformer — attention as a difference of two softmaxes

source.title: Differential Transformer
source.authors: Ye, Dong, Xia, Sun, Zhu, Huang, Wei (Microsoft / Tsinghua)

problem: Softmax 'over-allocates attention to irrelevant context' — attention noise that hurts retrieval, in-context learning and hallucination, and creates activation outliers.
idea: attention = softmax(Q₁K₁ᵀ) − λ·softmax(Q₂K₂ᵀ) with learnable λ and per-head GroupNorm — noise cancellation.
buys: Claims ~65% of the parameters or tokens to match a Transformer's loss; better needle retrieval, ICL and order robustness; fewer outliers
costs: ~5–12% lower throughput (−9/−12% at 3B, −5/−6% at 13B); runs on stock FlashAttention with two calls, a customised kernel is optional; evidence to ~13B
Zero saving on KV or context; not retrofittable; no frontier adoption found

chatbot2k.why: new pretraining run where retrieval / hallucination matter

pickWhen.verdict: A quality proposal in an efficiency decade; interesting, unshipped.

name: DuoAttention — retrieval heads vs streaming heads

source.title: DuoAttention: Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference with Retrieval and Streaming Heads
source.authors: Xiao et al. (MIT / Tsinghua / SJTU / NVIDIA)

problem: Only a minority of heads ('retrieval heads') need the full KV; the rest only need sink + recent window.
idea: Learn a per-head gate on synthetic passkey data; give retrieval heads full KV and streaming heads a sink+window cache.
buys: ~2.5× memory / ~2.2× decode speedup on MHA (≈1.6× / 1.5× on GQA); 3.3M tokens on one A100 with quantisation
costs: Offline optimisation per model; fixed split, not query-adaptive; two cache layouts complicate paged serving

coding128k.why: serving pretrained MHA/GQA models with long contexts on limited memory

pickWhen.verdict: The per-head version of what Gemma does per layer; bridges eviction and architecture.

name: Star Attention

source.title: Star Attention: Efficient LLM Inference over Long Sequences

oneLiner: Two-phase block-local prefill + global query attention for distributed long-context inference.

name: Gated DeltaNet — gating + the delta rule

source.title: Gated Delta Networks: Improving Mamba2 with Delta Rule

problem: Gating (Mamba-2) forgets fast but updates crudely; the delta rule (DeltaNet) updates precisely but cannot forget. Wanted both, with a hardware-parallel training algorithm.
idea: S_t = α_t (I − β_t k_t k_tᵀ) S_{t−1} + β_t v_t k_tᵀ: a data-dependent decay α on top of the erase-then-write delta update, trained chunkwise.
buys: 'Consistently surpasses Mamba2 and DeltaNet' on LM, in-context retrieval, length extrapolation and long-context; hybrids with sliding-window or Mamba-2 layers improve further
Constant-size state → O(1) KV per token; Qwen claims ~10× decode throughput vs Qwen3-32B at long context
The linear layer frontier models actually ship (Qwen3-Next, Kimi Linear's KDA)
costs: Still short of full softmax on exact recall — production uses 3:1 hybrids with real attention layers
Custom chunkwise kernels; lower training MFU than FlashAttention at short sequences
Fixed state bounds very-long-document fidelity; serving and quantisation ecosystem is young

chatbot2k.why: softmax is simpler and stronger at 4–8K

coding128k.why: as the majority layer of a hybrid

agent1m.why: 256K–1M agentic / long-generation workloads where decode throughput and KV dominate

pickWhen.verdict: The 1960 delta rule + a 2023 gate + a 2024 kernel = the layer 2025's hybrids are made of. Right at long context in a hybrid; wrong as the only attention.

name: Titans — neural long-term memory learned at test time

source.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time

problem: Attention is short-term memory; what plays long-term memory beyond the window?
idea: An MLP memory updated online by the gradient of a 'surprise' loss with momentum and decay (forgetting), combined with attention as context / gate / layer.
buys: >2M-token needle claims; O(1) memory per token at inference; beats Mamba-2 / DeltaNet-class baselines at ≤760M
costs: Per-chunk gradient steps at inference; immature kernels; no public weights; small-scale evidence

pickWhen.verdict: The endpoint of the DeltaNet / test-time-training line: memory as weights trained at inference.
